newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see Petrobras in Austrian schillings.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see Petrobras in Austrian schillings.

text.p: Petrobras grabbed headlines on Monday by launching its first Austrian schilling bond on a day when the eight-year issue was one of the primary market's few notable transactions.
Creditanstalt, the lead manager, said the 1.25 billion schilling 9.00 percent notes, priced at 99.875, yielded 320 basis points over Austrian governement paper.

A syndicate manager at the lead in Vienna said the deal was targeted primarily at Austrian retail investors to whom it expected to sell around two thirds of the deal, with the balance being taken up largely by Austrian institutions.
Creditanstalt said early sales were good, although a retail-targeted deal such as this took time to fully place.

Petrobras' debut in schillings followed previous deals from Argentina, Venezuela and Pemex, which introduced LatAm credits to Austrian investors. Creditanstalt expected more LatAm names would emerge in schillings in 1997, given the attraction to retail investors of this high coupon segment of the market.
Elsewhere today, Slovak Slovenska Sporitelna launched an $80 million 10-year FRN via Merrill Lynch.
The Slovenska Sporitelna notes pay three-month LIBOR plus 125 basis points rising to 300 b.p. after five years if a call at par is not exercised.
Cie Parisienne de Reescompte added 200 million French francs to the 1.0 billion franc 10-year TEC-10 deal it originally launched on December 9.
Business during the rest of the week was expected to remain confined to league table-related activity and a few small structured deals from LatAm borrowers.
Mainstream primary market business will remain at a virtual standstill until after the year-end break.
Last week's activity brought the volume of international bonds launched this year to around $665 billion, $200 billion more than last year's record-breaking total.
